_meta.description: sanitizeLLMOutput() ground truth (src/services/translation/llm-output.js, LLM engine overhaul Fase 2). Two sections: `cases` are inputs that MUST be transformed a specific way (a real problem the sanitizer exists to catch), `mustNotChange` are legitimate LLM outputs that MUST survive byte-identical — these are the non-negotiable half per the plan's rollback/risk section, since a false positive here looks like a Tuhua bug, not an LLM one.
_meta.fields: sourceLangCode/targetLangCode use Tuhua's internal codes (ja/zh/ko/ru/en/es/...). finishReason mirrors the OpenAI-compatible API's finish_reason ('stop'|'length'|null). expectedActions is compared as a set (order-independent); omit it to skip that check.

cases.note: The real bug found by Lyca (Nekopara Vol.1 session, ronda 4): a Clipboard hook briefly grabbed an unrelated pasted paragraph as 'game text'; GPT refused in Spanish and it sailed to the overlay uncaught. Neither prior signal could fire — the refusal is SHORTER than the (unusually long) source, so 2a's disproportion check fails; Spanish shares the Latin script with the target, so 2b never applies. This needs the topic-vocabulary signal (2c), independent of either side's length.

mustNotChange.input: Lo escribí en mi cuaderno de notas.
mustNotChange.expectedText: Lo escribí en mi cuaderno de notas.
mustNotChange.note: The word 'notas' appears mid-sentence, not as a blank-line-separated trailing paragraph starting with 'Note:' — must not trigger stripped-trailing-note.

The plan's explicit false-positive case: a character genuinely saying this in-universe, proportionate in length to a short source line, in the expected target script — must survive as a normal translation, not a refusal.

A proper name can legitimately be identical pre/post translation. Source and target share the 'latin' expected script, so the passthrough check must not even run here — it can only be trusted when scripts genuinely differ.

mustNotChange.input: Ella dijo que no puedo ayudar con eso y se fue enojada.
mustNotChange.sourceText: 彼女は私が手伝えないと言って怒って去った。
mustNotChange.expectedText: Ella dijo que no puedo ayudar con eso y se fue enojada.
mustNotChange.note: The unconditional refusal patterns are anchored to the whole string (short lead-in only, sentence must end there) precisely so real dialogue that mentions the same clause mid-paragraph, then keeps going, survives untouched.

mustNotChange.input: Lo siento, no puedo ir a la fiesta, tengo mucho contenido que estudiar para el examen.
mustNotChange.sourceText: ごめん、パーティーに行けない、試験のために勉強することがたくさんあるんだ。
mustNotChange.expectedText: Lo siento, no puedo ir a la fiesta, tengo mucho contenido que estudiar para el examen.
mustNotChange.note: 'contenido' is an everyday Spanish word (course material, not 'explicit content') — the topic signal (2c) is deliberately phrase-level ('proporcionar/generar contenido', not bare 'contenido') so ordinary dialogue using the word alone must survive untouched.
